=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27726-27738 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: In release_head_bound_needs_human_latches, the new scan between the bound latch ($b) and the newest autofix-cap latch ($i) counts any trusted latch comment in that range as a hold and never checks that comment's head against the PR's current head.
  WHY: Repeated autofix-cap comments on one stale head are a normal sequence (c1 labelled, then c2 and c3 on the same head A), and the label then binds to c1 through the fallback at 27713-27720. When the PR moves to head B, c2 matches the between scan, so every tick logs `later_needs_human_comment` and the label is never released. This is the permanent park that #9917 is meant to clear, and the previous round's fallback did release it. All reviewers rated this MAJOR, mapped here to high.
- scripts/review_autofix_step_post_review_blocked_comment.sh:121 | severity=critical | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: CI reports a shellcheck failure in the script.
  WHY: The reviewer says syntax or structural issues stop the script from passing automated linting. Its BLOCKER rating is mapped here to critical. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash rejected this finding: line 121 is a comment, no rule is named, the head check-run reports failed_count 0, and the last run modified no shell script.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "Release it when the head moves ... accept this comment as a third latch kind, with reason autofix_cap_head_moved", with tests for "autofix-cap release on a head move, with and without the head marker"
  expected_change_site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh release_head_bound_needs_human_latches (fallback-binding block, lines 27711-27738) and tests/test_needs_human_head_latch_release.py
  confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  EVIDENCE: No test covers a labelled default-heading comment followed by two or more default-heading comments on the same stale head after a head move, and the code as written never releases that case. The release-on-head-move requirement is therefore met only when the stale head has at most two latch comments.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:release_head_bound_needs_human_latches, lines 27726-27738 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The between-latches scan (`.key > $b and .key < $i ... contains("<!-- ai:autofix-cap-head:v1 ") or ...`, then `reason=later_needs_human_comment`) holds on any trusted latch between the bound latch and the newest latch, whatever its head. This contradicts the comment at 27726-27729, which says the intent is to catch a latch "on the PR's current head".
  WHY: scripts/review_autofix_step_post_review_blocked_comment.sh posts a default-heading comment with a head marker for every cap reason (lines 84-88) and adds the label (lines 183-189), which is a no-op when the label is already present. The crash-marker dedupe at lines 140-169 does not prevent repeats, so c1, c2 and c3 can all sit on head A. After a move to head B, the fallback at 27713-27720 binds to c1, c2 matches the scan, and the label is never released. This regresses the earlier fallback, and test `test_a_hold_between_the_bound_latch_and_the_autofix_cap_comment_is_kept` has no stale-head case. Suggested fix: hold on a between latch only when its hl_latch_candidates entry has `.head == $cur` or a head that is not 40-hex, add a regression test, and update the README row and the agents.d bullet to say "latches again on the current head".
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: "Release it when the head moves ... accept this comment as a third latch kind, with reason autofix_cap_head_moved" + tests for "autofix-cap release on a head move, with and without the head marker". Expected change site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh release_head_bound_needs_human_latches (lines 27711-27738) and tests/test_needs_human_head_latch_release.py. Evidence of absence: no test covers repeated autofix-cap latches on one stale head, and the code never releases that case. SEVERITY: MAJOR, ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3.
- Not carried forward: google_gemini's shellcheck finding at scripts/review_autofix_step_post_review_blocked_comment.sh:121. Line 121 is a comment, the check-run reports failed_count 0, and no rule is named.
- HARDENING: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh lines 27730-27735. Add `--argjson c "${hl_latch_candidates}" --arg cur "${hl_head}"` and split the predicate: re-assert headings and `ai:needs-human` mentions stay unconditional holds, and a latch holds only on a current-head or non-40-hex head. About 6 lines. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

  WHY: Each judge re-fire posts another autofix-cap comment with the same head marker. With three or more on a stale head while the PR is on a newer head, the scan logs `later_needs_human_comment` every tick and never releases, which regresses #9917.

The `ai:needs-human` mention and the two re-assert headings stay unconditional holds. About 6 lines. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2.

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:27730-27736 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The between-latches scan treats every trusted latch comment as a hold without checking its head.
  WHY: When several autofix-cap comments land on the same stale head, the label stays bound to the first comment while a later one is the newest latch. With the PR on a newer head, the intervening comment matches the scan, release is skipped every tick, and the stale `ai:needs-human` latch stays parked.

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:release_head_bound_needs_human_latches, lines 27726-27738 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The between-latches scan (`.key > $b and .key < $i` ... `reason=later_needs_human_comment`) counts any trusted latch between b and i as a hold without checking its head against the current head.
  WHY: The writer (scripts/review_autofix_step_post_review_blocked_comment.sh:84-88, 115-117) adds a head=A marker to every default-heading comment. In the failing chain, cap #1 is labelled and bound, cap #2 on the same head A is posted after the label event so the fallback jq at 27713-27720 cannot bind it, and cap #3 is the newest latch. Cap #2 then matches the predicate at 27734, so `NEEDS_HUMAN_HEAD_LATCH ... reason=later_needs_human_comment` is logged every tick and the label is never removed. Mixed latch kinds (round-cap, heal) behave the same way, and tests/test_needs_human_head_latch_release.py has no case for this.
- HARDENING: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh lines 27730-27735. Pass `--argjson c "${hl_latch_candidates}" --arg cur "${hl_head}"` and hold on a between latch only when its head is `.head == $cur` or not 40-hex. Keep the `ai:needs-human` mention and the re-assert headings as unconditional holds. Add a test with two autofix-cap comments on OLD_HEAD after the labelled one and the PR on NEW_HEAD, expecting a release. About 6 lines. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2.
- Rejected: google_gemini's shellcheck finding on scripts/review_autofix_step_post_review_blocked_comment.sh:121. No file or rule is named, and the check-run for head 2761c8e0989d151e6a7535ff9bbaae6363ecbdca reports failed_count: 0. The prior shellcheck `--severity=error` run was clean, and the last run modified no shell script.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
